title: Fast logic?: Examining the time course assumption of dual process theory
claims_supported: Initial deadline/load-constrained responses could be logically correct across four experiments.
Immediate processing is not necessarily an erroneous heuristic awaiting correction.
limitations: Restricted reasoning tasks, not a universal model of human cognition.
Does not establish equivalence between human processes and LLM computation.

title: The Mythical Number Two
claims_supported: The article challenges alignment of efficiency, awareness, intentionality and controllability into two process types.
limitations: Opinion/critical synthesis, not counted as an original empirical experiment.
Does not refute every task-specific dual-process model.

title: Uncertainty-based competition between prefrontal and dorsolateral striatal systems for behavioral control
claims_supported: Arbitration can compare estimated uncertainty of cached and model-based values.
Search approximation costs and learning efficiency can change which controller is favored.
limitations: Normative model with approximate uncertainty rather than identification of a unique neural mechanism.
Original anatomical assignments are hypotheses.
Not a safety guarantee for selecting software actions.

title: Model-Based Influences on Humans' Choices and Striatal Prediction Errors
claims_supported: Choice behavior contained model-based and model-free influences.
Striatal BOLD prediction-error signals contained model-based information.
limitations: BOLD is not direct dopamine recording.
Small task and fitted algorithm family do not uniquely identify all possible mechanisms.
The experiment did not show a trend toward progressive habit formation.

title: Neural Computations Underlying Arbitration between Model-Based and Model-free Learning
sections_inspected: Indexed reliability correlates and model comparisons
claims_supported: The model allocates control according to reliability estimated from prediction-error history.
Inferior lateral prefrontal and frontopolar activity covaried with reliability-related signals.
limitations: Direct PMC access returned a verification page; complete methods and supplement were not read directly.
fMRI covariation and model comparison do not prove a universal arbiter.
Exact reproduction requires obtaining complete methods before implementation.

title: When Does Model-Based Control Pay Off?
claims_supported: Common two-step variants need not yield higher reward for greater model-based control.
The redesigned task induced a clearer tradeoff and greater model-based reliance.
limitations: Conclusions concern the tested tasks and parameterization.
A benchmark can distinguish controllers without measuring value of additional computation.
Code repository link verified in paper; code was not executed.

title: Cortical and Subcortical Contributions to Stop Signal Response Inhibition: Role of the Subthalamic Nucleus
claims_supported: Stopping-related activity involved inferior frontal cortex and the vicinity of the subthalamic nucleus in two fMRI experiments.
Hyperdirect implementation was proposed for further investigation.
limitations: Direct PMC access challenged; full paper was not directly read.
Activation does not establish necessity, sufficiency, or a unique anatomical pathway.
Spatial localization around STN was explicitly qualified by authors.

title: Surprise disrupts cognition via a fronto-basal ganglia suppressive mechanism
claims_supported: Unexpected events impaired working-memory performance and recruited stopping-associated signals.
Subthalamic recordings supplied convergent evidence in Parkinson's patients.
limitations: Intracranial patient sample does not directly generalize to all populations.
Attention/detection and inhibition interpretations require care.
Does not prescribe globally stopping every surprising software event.

title: Activation of Subthalamic Nucleus Stop Circuit Disrupts Cognitive Performance
claims_supported: STN activation slowed responses and increased errors in delayed match-to-position.
STN inhibition attenuated surprise-related slowing without rescuing errors and itself impaired performance.
limitations: Motor, task-engagement and memory contributions are not fully disentangled.
Mouse task does not validate a software cancellation architecture.
Fast interruption and preserved state must be evaluated independently.

title: Sensory Prediction Errors Drive Cerebellum-Dependent Adaptation of Reaching
claims_supported: Comparing shooting and pointing conditions implicated sensory prediction error rather than the availability of online correction in the tested adaptation.
Seven cerebellar participants were impaired compared with seven matched controls.
limitations: Small motor-adaptation sample.
Sensory prediction error is distinct from reward error or target error.
Transfer to software consequence prediction is an engineering analogy.

title: Predictive coding in the visual cortex: a functional interpretation of some extra-classical receptive-field effects
claims_supported: A hierarchical prediction/residual model reproduced selected visual receptive-field effects.
The paper acknowledges alternative recurrent mechanisms.
limitations: Not proof that all cortex implements predictive coding.
Does not establish active inference or goal selection by prediction error alone.
No general software or AGI performance result follows.

title: Context-dependent computation by recurrent dynamics in prefrontal cortex
claims_supported: Population dynamics and a trained recurrent network accounted for context-dependent selection and integration.
Early exclusion of all irrelevant sensory input was not necessary in the proposed mechanism.
limitations: Two monkeys; most units recorded across different sessions.
Model sufficiency does not establish exclusivity.
No direct validation for software task memory.

title: A hierarchy of intrinsic timescales across primate cortex
claims_supported: Datasets from 26 monkeys and seven areas showed a hierarchical ordering of intrinsic timescales.
Association areas generally had longer timescales than sensory areas.
limitations: Population autocorrelation timescale is not a fixed biological decision deadline.
Cross-dataset/task differences require caution.
Does not identify exactly two control timescales.

title: Interacting Adaptive Processes with Different Timescales Underlie Short-Term Motor Learning
claims_supported: A two-rate adaptation model distinguished error sensitivity and retention.
Spontaneous recovery was predicted and tested in reaching adaptation.
limitations: Latent fitted processes do not identify two unique neural populations.
Learning timescales do not map directly to System 1 and System 2.
Does not imply a two-state model will suffice for software.

title: Why There Are Complementary Learning Systems in the Hippocampus and Neocortex: Insights From the Successes and Failures of Connectionist Models of Learning and Memory
claims_supported: Rapid episodic storage and gradual interleaved structural learning address competing learning demands.
Reinstatement/interleaving can reduce interference in the modeled systems.
limitations: Simplified connectionist models and broad theoretical synthesis.
Not evidence that neocortex always learns every fact slowly.
Offline skill promotion is an engineering inference, not the paper's software result.

title: Prioritized memory access explains planning and hippocampal replay
claims_supported: Expected benefit of a backup decomposes into gain and need in the proposed model.
Prioritized backups qualitatively reproduce selected replay phenomena.
limitations: Not a demonstrated efficient algorithm for finding the optimal memory.
Simulated navigation does not establish the biological mechanism.
Code repository was located but not executed.

title: Uncertainty, Neuromodulation, and Attention
claims_supported: The framework distinguishes expected cue unreliability from unexpected context change.
It proposes roles for acetylcholine and norepinephrine in those computations.
limitations: Neurotransmitter assignments are theoretical, not established one-to-one labels.
No direct software action-safety claim.
A single confidence score collapses distinctions that require separate evaluation.

title: Rational regulation of learning dynamics by pupil-linked arousal systems
claims_supported: Pupil measures covaried with modeled process instability, reliability and belief updating.
The paper reports an arousal manipulation influencing updating.
limitations: Direct PMC access challenged; complete methods not directly read.
Pupil size is an indirect physiological measure.
Does not establish a unique chemical implementation of uncertainty.

title: A critical role for the right fronto-insular cortex in switching between central-executive and default-mode networks
claims_supported: Right fronto-insular activity was associated with switching-related network patterns across the reported experiments.
limitations: Direct follow-up full-text reads failed or returned verification pages.
Directionality in observational BOLD is not equivalent to intervention causality.
No single-switch or LLM-to-default-mode identity follows.

title: A neuronal model of a global workspace in effortful cognitive tasks
sections_inspected: Workspace architecture and Stroop simulation rationale
claims_supported: The model coordinates specialized processors through a proposed global workspace.
Simulated recruitment varies with task acquisition, effort and errors.
limitations: A computational proposal, not a demonstration of software consciousness.
Does not show a central software blackboard is a faithful cortical implementation.
Must not be used as an AGI criterion.

title: Adversarial testing of global neuronal workspace and integrated information theories of consciousness
claims_supported: Preregistered multimodal experiments tested selected divergent predictions of GNW and IIT.
The published report supports some predictions while challenging aspects of both theories.
limitations: Complete methods and supplements were not directly obtained in this pass.
Does not settle all versions of either theory.
Provides no validated consciousness or AGI assessment for software.

title: Prefrontal cortex as a meta-reinforcement learning system
claims_supported: Slow reinforcement learning across tasks can train recurrent dynamics for rapid within-task adaptation.
Within-task adaptation can occur without changing the trained weights.
limitations: Institutional author manuscript was inspected; detailed version differences from final article were not audited.
Agreement with selected phenomena does not causally establish the full brain algorithm.
Transfer outside the training task distribution remains an independent software question.
